turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey, good to have you here. How are you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have six minutes to change trains tomorrow. Is that crazy?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Tight, but often fine if both trains are at the same station and on time. Is it one ticket for the whole trip?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, and another thing. My nan is leaving her big house and nobody knows what to do with all her furniture.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me walk you through all the options, then you can tell me what you think.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A house clearance company could take it all in one day, but we'd get almost nothing for it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My cousin wants to sell the nice pieces online one by one, which could make money but take months.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or we split it between the family and donate whatever's left to the hospice shop.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Splitting it between the family first feels right, since some pieces will mean a lot to people. Then a hospice shop for the rest is quick and kind, and you can still sell anything really valuable.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then if you miss the connection because of a delay, you're usually allowed on the next train without paying again.
